description: A1 JWT-auth-finder ground truth for erev0s/VAmPI. VAmPI signs HS256 with the weak secret 'random' and verifies signatures on decode. So a weak-secret-brute forgery (sub=admin signed with 'random') is accepted and escalates identity; an alg=none forgery is correctly REJECTED (a held-out decoy); and a public endpoint is reachable anonymously (another decoy). Scenarios are scored by whether the JwtAuthFinder returns Verified.

vulnerabilities.rationale: config.py sets SECRET_KEY='random'. The finder brute-forces a small wordlist, signs an HS256 token with sub='admin' using 'random', and GET /me returns the admin record (admin@mail.com, admin:true). The control identity (name2) sees only mail2@mail.com and the anonymous caller gets 401 — so the forged token reached data neither could.

decoys.rationale: VAmPI's decode_auth_token verifies the HS256 signature with SECRET_KEY. An alg=none / unsigned token claiming sub='admin' is REJECTED (401, 'Invalid token'), so the forged token never reaches admin data. A correctly-rejecting endpoint the finder must NOT flag.

/users/v1 (get_all_users) is unauthenticated and lists every user incl. admin@mail.com. The forged token 'works' but the anonymous caller ALSO receives admin@mail.com, so it is not an auth bypass — the finder must NOT flag it.
